decision_tracks.A_preserve_exact_ir_branch: Keep exact Y^(3/2); use a nonzero-gradient local background for force-sector perturbation theory and do not call it the homogeneous cosmological 2-to-2 amplitude.
decision_tracks.B_preserve_homogeneous_analytic_amplitud: Choose a smooth completion and a crossover sigma; accept and test the resulting modification of the deep-IR law.

projected_hessian_only.assessment: NOT_RECOMMENDED: it is nonzero for homogeneous psi on an evolving FRW background.
projected_hessian_only.difference: -theta Q relative to D_mu D^mu psi

selected_rest_space_laplacian.boundary: Track A adopts this operator for the next derivation.
selected_rest_space_laplacian.operator: Delta_U psi := D_mu D^mu psi = h^{mu nu} nabla_mu nabla_nu psi + theta Q
reasons: generally covariant scalar built from g, U and psi
reduces to the Stage-A spatial Laplacian for constant U
annihilates fields homogeneous on the aether rest space
has a purely spatial second-derivative principal part
in aether-unitary ADM it is the intrinsic leaf Laplacian

spacetime_divergence.assessment: VIABLE_BUT_NONMINIMAL: it is divergence-form but adds an acceleration/lapse-gradient coupling.
spacetime_divergence.difference: +a^mu D_mu psi relative to D_mu D^mu psi

scientific_boundary: The regulator comparison identifies the operator now adopted by Track A. No option simultaneously keeps the exact asymptotic Y^(3/2) law at Y=0 and supplies an ordinary analytic zero-background vertex. UVIR-003 and MAT-001 therefore remain open.
selected_decision: Track A: retain exact Y^(3/2), adopt D_mu D^mu psi, and assign force perturbation theory to a declared nonzero-gradient local background.

verified_identities.label: D_mu D^mu psi = hessian_perp + theta Q
nabla_mu(h^{mu nu} nabla_nu psi) = D^2 psi + a.D psi
D^2 psi vanishes for homogeneous psi on flat FRW

verified_nonzero_background_series.label: nonzero-gradient Y^(3/2) expansion through quartic order

verified_smoothing_series.label: unsubtracted smoothing generates a canonical Y term

exact_zero_gradient_branch.use: classical nonlinear boundary-value problems; not a standard zero-background perturbative S-matrix vertex

nonzero_gradient_background.cost: background selects a spatial direction; the quartic coefficient contains 1/|grad psi_0| and has no regular zero-gradient limit
nonzero_gradient_background.use: local weak-field response, not isotropic FRW scattering

smooth_linear_subtracted.benefit: analytic at Y=0 without a canonical Y term; the leading interaction is quartic in spatial gradients
smooth_linear_subtracted.cost: introduces a crossover scale and replaces the exact deep-IR Y^(3/2) law by Y^2

smooth_with_linear_term.benefit: analytic at Y=0 and supplies quadratic spatial stiffness
smooth_with_linear_term.cost: the generated (3/2) sigma Y term dominates in the deep IR and changes the target asymptotic branch
